source: Canadian National Autism Foundation, cnaf.net/provinceres.html; each entry checked on its own website

entries.name: Hann Psychological Services
entries.description: A private psychology practice in Halifax, led by psychologist Gerald Hann, that does autism (ASD) assessments for children, teens and adults, along with psychoeducational and ADHD assessments and therapy. An autism assessment includes interviews, observation and a written report with recommendations.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.address: 5991 Spring Garden Road, Suite 585 Halifax, Nova Scotia B3H 1Y6
entries.evidence: Dr. Hann specializes in comprehensive autism assessments and diagnosis.
entries.notes: Address is from the site's contact block (Halifax Professional Centre); the site lists no phone or email, and referrals go through online self-referral and professional-referral forms. The About page says one clinician offers virtual treatment by video. Site footer says © 2023. CNAF links to this page twice (an image link and a text link).

entries.name: Green Leaf Psychological Services
entries.description: A private psychology clinic in Halifax that does autism (ASD) assessments for children and teens (ages 6 to 18) and adults (19 and older), as well as ADHD, learning disorder and other assessments, and in-person or virtual therapy. Each assessment ends with a written report and recommendations.
entries.cost_note: Assessments, including autism assessments, are charged at $230 per hour, with an estimate given before starting; not covered by MSI, but usually covered by private insurance.
entries.address: 1526 Dresden Row, Suite 602, Halifax, Nova Scotia B3J 3K3
entries.evidence: Our adult autism testing is for those 19 and older and our child autism assessments start at age 6.
entries.notes: As of 18 Oct 2026 the site says it is not taking new child or adult autism/ASD assessments because of a full caseload (Contact page lists both as "Not Currently Accepting"). CNAF links to the older adult page (autism-asd-assessment-halifax.html), which still loads; the site menu now points to this page. Phone and address are from the Contact page; the email there is hidden by an email-protection script, so it is left out.

entries.name: Nova Scotia Student Assistance
entries.description: The Government of Nova Scotia's loan and grant program for post-secondary students. One application covers both Nova Scotia and Canada loans and grants, including grants for students with disabilities, which may need extra documentation.
entries.cost_note: Grants do not need to be repaid; loans must be repaid starting six months after leaving school. The site does not mention an application fee.
entries.evidence: When you apply for Nova Scotia Student Assistance for Full-Time Studies, you are applying for both Loans and Grants, from both the Government of Nova Scotia and the Government of Canada.
entries.notes: Apply and send questions online through MyPATH, by phone (toll-free 1-800-565-8420), or walk in at The Thompson Building, 1256 Barrington Street, Halifax. CNAF links to several Student Assistance pages (home, loans and grants, calculated need, eligibility, obligations, 0% interest), all current, and to a Medical Assessment form that is now 404. Disability grants are handled by Post-Secondary Accessibility Services (separate entry).

entries.name: Post-Secondary Accessibility Services (PSAS)
entries.description: A Nova Scotia Department of Advanced Education office that runs the Canada Student Grant for Students with Disabilities and the grant for disability-related services and equipment (such as tutors, note-takers and assistive technology) for post-secondary students. Students need a verified disability, Nova Scotia residency, and a current Nova Scotia Student Assistance application with assessed financial need.
entries.cost_note: Grants are non-repayable ($2,800 per academic year for the CSG-D; services and equipment grants by separate application). The site does not mention any fee.
entries.evidence: These grants provide financial assistance to eligible post-secondary students to help reduce or remove barriers to post-secondary education.
entries.notes: CNAF links to "Nova Scotia Post-Secondary Disability Services" (http://psds.ednet.ns.ca/) and its Services and Equipment Grant page; that no longer works (the domain now shows an unrelated Community-Based Learning page and the grant page is 404). The same grants are now run by Post-Secondary Accessibility Services at https://novascotia.ca/post-secondary-accessibility-services/ (the site does not mention the old name). Office: Thompson Building, 1256 Barrington Street, 5th Floor, Halifax.

entries.name: Easter Seals Nova Scotia
entries.description: A charity that supports Nova Scotians with disabilities through Camp Tidnish (an overnight summer camp), New Leaf Enterprises (job skills and supported employment for youth and adults), Take PART recreation and sport programs, and Assisted Mobility programs that help people get wheelchairs, assistive devices and health care equipment.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.address: 22 Fielding Ave Dartmouth, Nova Scotia Canada B3B 1E2
entries.evidence: We have programs that help Nova Scotians with disabilities access wheelchairs, assistive devices and health care equipment.
entries.notes: Main number 902-453-6000; program staff are on extensions listed on the Contact page, which gives only program and staff emails (no general address). There is also a Yarmouth office. Charity registration number is in the site footer.

entries.name: Housing Repair and Accessibility Program
entries.description: A Government of Nova Scotia program that helps low- and moderate-income homeowners pay for critical home repairs and for accessibility adaptations, such as ramps, accessible bathrooms and kitchens, for a household member with a disability or reduced ability. Each stream can fund up to $18,000 (part grant, part forgivable loan), with an optional repayable loan for larger projects.
entries.cost_note: There is no cost to apply; funding is a grant plus a forgivable loan, and the applicant or other sources pay any remaining balance.
entries.evidence: The program also provides funding for accessibility adaptations (upgrades) to help people with disabilities and seniors stay in their homes.
entries.notes: CNAF names the Access-A-Home Program and links to http://housing.novascotia.ca/, which now redirects to novascotia.ca's general housing programs page; there, help with accessibility adaptations is this program. The page does not mention the Access-A-Home name, so a reviewer may want to confirm it replaced Access-A-Home. Homeowners must have owned and lived in the home for at least a year and meet income and property-value limits; apply online or by mail.

entries.name: Disability Support Program (DSP)
entries.description: The Government of Nova Scotia's program for children, youth and adults with intellectual disabilities, long-term mental illness or physical disabilities. It funds community living options (such as Flex individualized funding, Independent Living Support and Alternative Family Support), day programs, and family support for children living at home.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost; financial eligibility rules are in the DSP Policy.
entries.evidence: The Disability Support Program (DSP) services children, youth and adults with intellectual disabilities, long-term mental illness and physical disabilities in a range of community supported living options and day programs.
entries.notes: To apply, call the toll-free number on the page. The department is now called Opportunities and Social Development. CNAF lists this page twice ("Disabilty Support Program" and "Government services for special needs"). Direct Family Support for Children and the day programs, which CNAF lists separately, have their own entries.

entries.name: Income Assistance (IA)
entries.description: Nova Scotia's Income Assistance program, part of Employment Support and Income Assistance (ESIA), gives money for basic needs such as food, clothing and shelter, and sometimes for special needs, to people who cannot financially support themselves or their family. Employment Support Services also offers programs to help clients learn skills and find work.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Income Assistance can help you if you are not able to financially support yourself or your family.
entries.notes: Apply by calling 1-877-424-1177 or contacting a local office (How to Apply page); active clients can submit income statements online. The department is now called Opportunities and Social Development.

entries.name: Nova Scotia Child Benefit (NSCB)
entries.description: A monthly payment from the Government of Nova Scotia to lower-income families to help with the cost of raising children under 18. It is paid together with the federal Canada Child Benefit and is based on the family's income tax return, so families do not have to apply.
entries.cost_note: A benefit paid to eligible families based on family net income; the page does not mention any cost.
entries.evidence: In July 2023, government is increasing the Nova Scotia Child Benefit (NSCB) amount eligible families receive to help with the cost of raising children under 18 years of age.
entries.notes: The page's rates are "as of July 2023" (families with adjusted net income under $34,000) and it has not been updated since, so amounts may have changed.

entries.name: Community Inclusion and Day Programming (Disability Support Program)
entries.description: Day programs for youth and adults with disabilities, funded by Nova Scotia's Disability Support Program and run by non-profit organizations in every region. Programs vary and can include skill development, supported employment, social enterprises, recreation and retirement activities; the page lists providers by community.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: The Disability Support Program (DSP) supports adults and youth with disabilities to participate in meaningful activities, and in being a part of their community.
entries.notes: CNAF lists this as "Adult Service Centres" (AdultServiceCentres.html), which now redirects here. Programs are self-referral and some have waitlists; contact each provider directly (the page lists about 40 providers with addresses and phone numbers).

entries.name: Direct Family Support for Children (DFSC)
entries.description: Nova Scotia Disability Support Program funding that helps families care for a child with a disability at home, mainly by paying for respite so caregivers get scheduled breaks; Enhanced Family Support for Children (EFSC) adds more funding for families who qualify. The child must be under 19, live at home and have a qualifying disability diagnosed by an approved clinician, and family income must meet the program guidelines.
entries.cost_note: A funding program with family income guidelines; the page does not mention any cost.
entries.evidence: Direct Family Support for Children (DFSC) and Enhanced Family Support for Children (EFSC) provide funding to enable families to support their child with a disability at home.
entries.notes: Qualifying diagnoses listed are an intellectual developmental disability (mild or moderate with a significant behavioural challenge, or severe), a significant physical disability, or a dual diagnosis; autism on its own is not named. Call 1-877-424-1177 or visit a Community Services office.

entries.name: Nova Scotia Human Rights Commission
entries.description: An independent Nova Scotia government agency that administers the Nova Scotia Human Rights Act. People who have experienced discrimination or harassment based on a protected characteristic can contact it for information or send an online inquiry form to start its dispute resolution process.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Whether you are contacting the Commission because you have experienced harassment or discrimination based on a protected characteristic, or just looking for information, staff are here to support you.
entries.notes: Offices in Halifax (5657 Spring Garden Road), Sydney and Digby; local Halifax number 902-424-4111. The home page features the remedy in Disability Rights Coalition v Province of Nova Scotia. CNAF also links to the contact page as a separate item.

entries.name: Office of the Ombudsman (Nova Scotia)
entries.description: An independent, non-partisan office that investigates complaints from people who believe they were treated unfairly by a Nova Scotia provincial or municipal government department, agency, board or commission. People are asked to try that body's own complaint or appeal process first, then can file a complaint online.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: The Ombudsman considers and investigates complaints from people who believe they have been treated unfairly when using government services, or when they believe a policy or procedure has not been followed correctly or is unfair.
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://novascotia.ca/ombu/, which now redirects to ombudsman.novascotia.ca. Within HRM call 902-424-6780; office at 5657 Spring Garden Road, Suite 200, Halifax. The site has youth and seniors resources.

entries.name: Therapeutic Riding Program (Halifax Lancers)
entries.description: A volunteer-run therapeutic horseback riding program at the Halifax Lancers, a non-profit riding school in Halifax, for people over age 5 with a diagnosis such as autism, cerebral palsy or a learning disability. Six-week sessions run in spring and fall, with 45-minute lessons led by an instructor and volunteers.
entries.cost_note: The site says payment is requested at registration; it does not list the fee.
entries.evidence: We continue to be affiliated with the IWK, and also offer horseback riding to other members of the community with disabilities.
entries.notes: CNAF lists H.A.L.T.R. (Halifax Area Leisure and Therapeutic Riding) and links to http://www.bengallancers.com/haltr.html; that no longer works (it redirects to a 404 on halifaxlancers.com). The organisation now uses https://www.halifaxlancers.com/therapeutic-riding. Riders join a waitlist and need a medical referral and an assessment meeting.

entries.name: Nova Scotia Services (Bartimaeus)
entries.description: Bartimaeus, a Canadian company founded in 1988, provides behavioural support services in Nova Scotia. Its Residential Resource offers short-term respite or specialized support stays for children, adolescents and adults with complex behaviours, and it also offers in-home and community family support, mentoring for youth moving into adulthood, and counselling for parents.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.address: 117 Dominion Street, Truro, Nova Scotia B2N 3P6
entries.evidence: In Nova Scotia, Bartimaeus Residential Resource is available for children, adolescents and adults requiring respite care, or temporary specialized support, due to behavioural difficulties.
entries.notes: Head office is in Burlington, Ontario; the Truro address and phone are its Maritimes administrative office and coordinator (Contact page). The site says its specialized behavioural support is provided throughout the Maritime provinces, including to agencies, schools and hospitals. CNAF links to the general About page and also lists Bartimaeus on its Prince Edward Island page.
